seo.title: Avesta Proof: CRA, ISO 27001 & IEC 62443 evidence | Avesta Tech
seo.description: Avesta Proof maps your scan results to three standards, prioritises exploited CVEs and signs every report. Local-first. Your code never leaves you.

sections.heading: Turn code scans into audit evidence.
sections.sub: Avesta Proof scans a repository, maps what it finds to ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443-4-1 and the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and produces a signed, tamper-evident report with a fix for every finding. Your code never leaves your machine.

rows.heading: A weekly verdict per standard.
rows.body: Pass, partial, warn, fail or not-assessed for every mapped control. Each finding names the file, the line and the fix. Run it on every pull request and on a weekly schedule, because new CVEs appear even when your code does not change.

rows.heading: Know what attackers are using today.
rows.body: Avesta Proof checks every dependency vulnerability against the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue and the FIRST EPSS score. You see the handful that matter now, not a wall of red.

rows.heading: Evidence an auditor can verify without trusting you.
rows.body: Every report has a SHA-256 fingerprint and an Ed25519 signature. Each scan links to the previous one in a ledger. Delete or edit an old scan and the chain breaks. Your auditor checks it with one command, offline.

rows.heading: Manual evidence that keeps itself honest.
rows.body: Record your pen test, threat model or design review as an attestation with a validity period. When it expires, the control turns red. Accepted risks need a reason, an approver and an end date, and they come back when that date passes.

rows.heading: Your CRA technical file, drafted from real data.
rows.body: Avesta Proof drafts the technical documentation structured on Annex VII of the Regulation, generates a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM, counts down to the key CRA dates and checks your declared support period. Your team completes and reviews the draft; we never pretend a draft is the finished file.

rows.heading: Answer security questionnaires in minutes.
rows.body: Share a one-page trust statement and a badge with customers. It shows your current verdict and links to evidence you choose to publish.

rows.heading: Local-first by design.
rows.body: The scan runs in your CI or on an air-gapped machine. Source code stays with you. Only signed results move.

rows: Code vulnerabilities in many languages, with bundled offline rules
C and C++ memory and logic errors
Dependency CVEs, container and infrastructure misconfiguration
SECURITY.md, SBOM, CI, lock files, dependency updates, licence, CODEOWNERS, .env files
sections.note: A scanner that does not apply (for example, no C files) is marked not-applicable and does not count against you.

sections.heading: Seven outputs from one run.
paragraphs: HTML report · signed JSON · SARIF for GitHub and GitLab code scanning · CycloneDX SBOM · trust statement · badge · CRA technical-file draft. PDF on request.

sections.heading: What Avesta Proof does not do.
items: Control mappings are indicative. A compliance expert should review them against the current standard text.
Automated tools miss design flaws and business-logic bugs. Pair them with threat modelling and pen tests; our services can help.
SBOM support today: Python, npm and Cargo lock files. Maven, Gradle, Go, yarn, pnpm and NuGet are on the roadmap.
There is no hosted dashboard yet. The signed JSON and the ledger are your data.
